judgement.summary: A single-concept plan ("the site is a wall section") that scrolls through a cut from skin to frame, with one genuine 3D moment — an exploded axonometric of the Calder Court wall build-up — plus project sections, a client-facing "How I Work" stretch, a timeline, and a direct contact close; by the final reply it is scrupulously honest about roles, the modelled 68% figure, image rights and the competition team. Its greatest weakness is structural rather than factual: the wall-section idea stays a metaphor for motion instead of becoming the page's form, the richest field-specific material (drawing-set order, RIBA stages, snag list, Swiss joints book) is demoted to one section and captions, there is no single 3D object carrying the scroll, and the hero offers no proof or route to contact for a visitor who does not scroll.

traps.evidence: "Calder Court (flagship) — The centrepiece"; hero "scrolling the mouse wheel literally retrofits the building in front of you. That's the thesis stated in motion" — no role or practice attribution.
"Then the heating-demand diagram, bars drawing themselves on scroll to land on '68% less.'"
"**Marta Kowalczyk**, Associate at Field & Rowe Architects"; timeline "Field & Rowe (Architect → Associate)" — never "Senior Architect", though the hero label is just "Architect".
"Before/after photo pairs (Tom Reid's 14 shots) on a scroll-driven slider"; "the real 1:5 wall build-up detail from Calder Court" — planned with no permission or credit.
"it's treated honestly as a competition entry: the six A1 boards, large and legible" — no mention of collaborators, in a site that is hers.

invented.claim: That Calder Court's render and winter gardens are a muted ochre or brick-terracotta — "one accent pulled from Calder Court's actual render/winter-garden colour"; no colour is stated anywhere in the material.

final.question: The site is a wall section. Architects cut through a building to show what it's really made of; scrolling down this site is scrolling through that cut — from outer skin to frame.

swap.reason: A wall-section scroll is a stock architect conceit and the hero artwork is admitted to be "new, generic artwork", so the concept would transfer unchanged to any retrofit architect's site.

backdrop.reason: The one 3D element is the wall build-up she herself detailed, revealed layer by layer with leader lines, so deleting it would lose the section's actual argument about her contribution, not ornament.

depth.reason: After the hero it is a run of project sections whose order is largely interchangeable, and the promised skin-to-frame progression never maps onto the parts.

clipart.reason: There is no single central object carrying the page — a generic layered hero graphic and a separate Calder axonometric are different, unconnected scenes.

honesty.reason: The final plan names the partner's concept and her project-architect scope, labels 68% as modelled with monitoring pending, gates Reid's photos and the practice's drawings behind permission and credit, and credits the competition team of four.

thirty_seconds.reason: The hero gives name, role and one line but explicitly offers no navigation and no proof, and contact sits only at the foot of the page.

plain_reader.reason: "Associate, Field & Rowe Architects" plus "I work on buildings that already exist" is plain to a homeowner and credible to an architect.
